The narrator's younger sister is already dead, and her death was not a suicide. The narrator deliberately wrote a note that would be read as the sister's own suicide note, because the narrator wants people to believe the sister died by suicide. But the note is really an expression of the narrator's own wish to die—not the sister's—and it is not being used to cover up a murder by the narrator, a killing by anyone else, an accident, or a natural death. The narrator was not forced by anyone and was not protecting another person from suspicion. In short: after the sister's non-suicidal death, the grieving narrator fabricated a false suicide note in the dead sister's name, projecting the narrator's own suicidal feelings into it so the death would be perceived as a suicide.

The narrator lived with the sister and came home after the sister was already dead, then wrote a note designed to be read as the sister's own suicide note. The narrator's aim was that the sister's death be treated or recorded as a suicide rather than its true cause. The note was easy to write because its content expressed the narrator's own wish to die—the narrator projected their own suicidal feelings onto the dead sister. This deception was not to cover a murder by the narrator, a killing by anyone else, an accident, illness, childbirth, assisted dying, a suicide pact, financial gain, or to protect another person; the narrator was not forced. Murder and other specific cause-of-death branches were repeatedly irrelevant, indicating the true cause is not the crux. The motive connecting the deception to the narrator's death wish remains the unresolved core: the note transforms the sister's death into a chosen suicide, mirroring the narrator's own desire to die.

The narrator's younger sister is genuinely dead and was already dead when the narrator came home, where they lived together. Her death was not a suicide, and it was not a killing by the narrator or by another person, nor an accident the narrator caused. The narrator deliberately wrote a note intended to be read as the dead sister's own suicide note, so that people—including the third person they lived with—would believe the sister had died by suicide. The note was easy to write because its text described the narrator's own wish to die: the narrator projected their own suicidal feelings onto the dead sister. The deception was not for money, not to protect anyone, not to cover a murder, and the narrator was not forced. The motive is tied to the narrator's own death wish—the note recasts the sister's non-suicidal death as a chosen suicide, mirroring the narrator's own desire to die—while also shaping how the death is perceived and officially treated.
